chapter_title: Designing an A/B Test with Students
learning_objective: The learner will identify the six parts of an A/B test design from a description of how each looks, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** ab-test-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the six parts of an A/B test design from a description of how each looks, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** A/B Test, Control Group, Treatment Group, Random Assignment, Pre-Test, Post-Test, Outcome Measure (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The two groups are formed by choice. (2) Only the post-test is needed. (3) The control group gets no lesson. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a design is a Remember-level task, and a picture of the whole flow from pool to comparison gives each part a place. The quiz asks the learner to recognize a part by its look. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing read from left to right. At the left is a circle of 24 identical small figures. An arrow leaves the circle and passes through a pair of dice. Beyond the dice the figures split into two equal clusters, an upper cluster of 12 holding a page with one dot and a lower cluster of 12 holding a page with two dots. Each cluster has a pencil-and-paper icon before it and another after it. At the right is a balance scale with a cluster on each pan. The six markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Student pool | The circle of identical figures at the left. | The students invited to take part. | Invite every student in the class, and record who agrees. | | 2 | Random assignment | The pair of dice on the arrow. | Chance decides who gets which version. | Sort by the pre-test, pair neighbors, and flip a coin inside each pair. | | 3 | Control group | The upper cluster holding the page with one dot. | The students who use the original version. | Treat them exactly like the other group in every way but the version. | | 4 | Treatment group | The lower cluster holding the page with two dots. | The students who use the improved version. | Give them nothing extra beyond the improved version. | | 5 | Pre-test and post-test | The pencil-and-paper icons before and after each cluster. | The same tests, given to both groups. | Use equivalent forms and the same conditions for both groups. | | 6 | Comparison | The balance scale at the right. | The two groups' learning gains are compared. | Compare the gains and not only the post-test scores. | **Provenance:** The six parts follow the chapter sections "A/B Test", "Random Assignment", "Control Group", "Treatment Group", "Pre-Test", "Post-Test", and "Outcome Measure". The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels it "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 6 in the order of the table, from left to right. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 6 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 6 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 6 correct on the first attempt". At 5 or more it adds "You can read the design of an A/B test." Below 5 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with six numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see a part of the design." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's eight-step method and its sections on groups, assignment, and tests describe the same six parts.
